method: Repair funds are editable savings contributions, not predicted annual bills. No comparable Australian model-by-model paid-repair dataset was verified. Defaults reflect age, warranty exposure and component prices; low/high figures are alternative savings budgets. Running costs before this fund are shown separately. Unspent money remains cash. Servicing, tyres and insured crashes are separate; a major battery or engine event can exceed the pool.

findings.title: Model Y: mixed reliability signals
findings.text: TÜV 2026 found significant defects in 17.3% of 2–3-year-old German Model Ys, especially suspension, brakes and lights. ADAC 2026 places Model Y among its strongest midsize roadside-breakdown performers. These measure different problems; neither provides Australian repair bills or a Juniper forecast.

findings.title: Australian repair prices support a buffer
findings.text: Whiteline lists an original-body upper-arm pair fitted with alignment at A$1,823 incl. GST; one offer, not a minimum. JPI estimates compressor replacement at A$2,000–4,000+. Neither provides failure frequency. Independent repair-fund estimates are A$1,000/year for original RWD/Long Range and A$700 for newer Juniper. These build contingency savings, not predicted repair spending.

findings.title: ICCU: check Australian cover before budgeting a bill
findings.text: Drive reports Australian manufacturer confirmation of 15-year/300,000-km ICCU cover: Ioniq 5 built 2 Apr 2021–14 Feb 2024 and EV6 MY22–24, from first registration. Confirm VIN-specific terms in writing; an overseas policy alone is insufficient. Eligible recalls and covered defects should not be charged as routine owner repairs.

findings.title: Breakdowns do not equal full repair costs
findings.text: ADAC 2026 flags German Ioniq 5 first registered 2022–23 and RAV4 2017–22 for roadside events. ICCU and 12V issues respectively are material context, but German incidents do not establish Australian out-of-pocket bills, every model year or the new RAV4 generation.
